newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: CS says Elektrowatt due diligence goes on.
newsitem.headline: CS says Elektrowatt due diligence goes on.

text.p: Credit Suisse Group said due diligence talks with Germany's Siemens were continuing over the industrial business of Elektrowatt, which the Swiss bank is selling to Siemens.

A Credit Suisse Group spokeswoman denied a Swiss newspaper report that claimed the due diligence results were being kept under wraps by the bank, which had earlier said the results would be made public in late April.
"Negotiations are part of due diligence and talks with Siemens are continuing," spokeswoman Karin Rhomberg told Reuters.
"We will inform the public after due diligence is completed," Rhomberg said. "We are not quite this far yet. It will certainly not take much longer."

CS Group, which had a 44.9 percent stake in Elektrowatt, agreed in December to sell the company after splitting it along its two main divisions -- industrial activities focused on building control systems and electrical power generation.
Due diligence for the power side was completed in March and confirmed the initial price of 265 Swiss francs per share set with the buyer, a consortium of Swiss and German utilities.
Siemens agreed to take the industrial side of Elektrowatt for 285 Swiss francs per share or about 1.1 billion Swiss francs.
Swiss weekly newspaper SonntagsZeitung wrote on Sunday that results of due diligence at Elektrowatt's industrial business were being deliberately withheld by CS Group.
The newspaper quoted unnamed sources close to the deal as saying they expected a lower price to emerge from the due diligence.
CS Group spokeswoman Rhomberg declined further comment on the newspaper report or on whether the sale price of 285 Swiss francs per share had been confirmed by the due diligence review.
